In Speaking and Writing about the Noble Companions (رضي الله عنهم), Let Us Uphold Adab and Choose Our Words with Care!

The Noble Companions (Ṣaḥābah, رضي الله عنهم) constitute the finest generation of this Ummah, as attested by the standards of the Qur’an and Sunnah. They were the first bearers and guardians of Islam, nurtured in the company of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They witnessed the religion firsthand and serve as exemplary models for the entire Ummah that came after them.

Their unparalleled contributions to the knowledge and practice of the Qur’an and Sunnah, their faith, sacrifices, sincerity, and moral character remain an everlasting source of inspiration for the Muslim Ummah. It was through them that the teachings of the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached subsequent generations. They carried the noble trust of this religion and faithfully transmitted it to those who came after them.

Alongside their exalted status and unparalleled excellence, however, it is important to remember that they were not prophets or messengers, nor were they ma‘ṣūm (معصوم)—infallible or divinely protected from all error. They were human beings.

Consequently, within the ordinary limits of human fallibility, some of them made mistakes, whether intentionally or unintentionally; certain decisions may have involved errors of judgment, and temporary lapses may have occurred on particular occasions. Some such incidents have been reported in the Qur’an and authentic Hadith.

At the same time, the Qur’an and Hadith also vividly reflect their sincere repentance, wholehearted return to Allah, steadfastness in faith, commitment to self-correction, and profound obedience to Him.

In fact, the occurrence of a mistake or lapse in the life of a Companion, simply because he or she was human, does not diminish their overall greatness or exalted standing. Rather, their firm faith, God-consciousness (taqwa), repentance, willingness to reform themselves, unwavering commitment to the truth, and extraordinary sacrifices and selfless devotion to the religion have established their place at an unparalleled height in history.

For this reason, it is inappropriate to call into question the standing of those whose status as Companions has been reliably and authentically established, or to pass negative judgments on their overall character on the basis of an error, shortcoming, or lapse that may have occurred during their lives.

If a particular incident warrants discussion for a legitimate scholarly purpose, it may certainly be examined. However, certain conditions must be met: the incident must be established through reliable and authentic narrations; its proper historical context and interpretation must be carefully examined; and the discussion must preserve the dignity of the Noble Companions and the adab (respectful conduct and proper etiquette) due to them.

In particular, it is unjustifiable to arrive at negative conclusions about a Companion’s entire life, faith, character, or standing on the basis of an isolated incident, a weak report, or a solitary narration.

Similarly, we should avoid words, adjectives, and turns of phrase that might, even unintentionally, cast a negative shadow over their overall standing. When speaking about the Noble Companions (رضي الله عنهم), accuracy of information is not the only consideration; proper linguistic etiquette and fairness in presentation are equally important.

Therefore, when evaluating any incident or narration concerning them, we must not focus exclusively on a single source or isolated event. Rather, we should consider the comprehensive perspective of the Qur’an and Sunnah, the established virtues of the Companion concerned, their faith and sacrifices, the authenticity of the incident, the context of the narration, and the explanations offered by the mufassirun (scholars of Qur’anic exegesis) and muḥaddithun (scholars of Hadith).

Only then can our discussions be simultaneously grounded in sound scholarship, fairness, and proper adab.

Discussions of mistakes or lapses that may have occurred in the lives of the Noble Companions should never be intended to diminish their standing. Rather, where such discussion is warranted, its purpose should be to understand and evaluate the relevant matter appropriately, on the basis of authentic knowledge, historical accuracy, and a balanced perspective informed by the Qur’an and Sunnah.

We may draw lessons from their mistakes or lapses, but in doing so, we must never lose sight of their overall standing, faith, sacrifices, and extraordinary contributions to the preservation and transmission of Islam.

The pursuit of truth is essential. Equally indispensable, however, is the preservation of respect, fairness, and restraint when presenting that truth concerning the Noble Companions (رضي الله عنهم).

Above all, our attitude towards the Noble Companions should be one of love, reverence, fairness, and adab.

When accepting and presenting narrations concerning them, our approach should be characterized by taḥqīq (rigorous verification), caution, balance, and objectivity.

For those who were among the principal bearers and custodians of our religion, our words about them should likewise be worthy of their exalted standing: truthful, measured, and respectful.

For a more detailed discussion, see Uṣūl al-Īmān, Volume 3, section on the Noble Companions (رضي الله عنهم).
